chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the twig (jaridah), whether it is placed beneath the garments or above them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Above the shirt and below the loins.' So I asked him (peace be upon him), 'From which side?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'On the right side.'

key_terms.الْجَرِيدَة: A small twig or piece of wood used in ritual washing
key_terms.الْخَاصِرَة: The loins or lower back area

ai.seo_question: Where exactly should the twig be placed during the ritual washing of the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise anatomical placement of the 'jaridah' (a small twig or piece of wood) used during the ritual washing (ghusl) of the deceased, specifying it should be placed above the shirt but below the loins, and positioned on the right side of the body. This detail reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on replicating the Prophet’s and Imams’ practices with exactitude, ensuring the ritual’s validity through adherence to specific physical markers. The right-side placement may symbolize honor and alignment with the natural posture of the deceased in preparation for burial.
